title: Quarterly Customer Engagement Orchestration — Stakeholder Prep & Facilitation Scripts
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic, repeatable orchestration for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) focused on proactive renewal influence, stakeholder alignment, and product roadmap input. It’s intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, and Customer Success leadership running 30–90 minute executive and operational QBRs.

Before-the-QBR checklist (72–48–24 hours cadence):
- 72h: Internal sync with AE/SE (owner: CSM) — confirm ask, contract dates, open tickets, recent outages/incidents, usage trends. Attach latest account snapshot.
- 48h: Stakeholder map & tailored invites (owner: CSM) — identify executive vs. operational attendees; include two objective asks per attendee.
- 24h: External pre-read + one-item prep (owner: CSM) — send 2–3 page pre-read: top metrics, wins, open risks, suggested agenda. Ask customer to add any discussion topics.
- Handouts to prepare: usage heatmaps, costs by route, two prompt quality examples, renewal timeline.

Stakeholder mapping (quick reference):
- Executive Sponsor — name: (e.g., Sarah K.) — prep: highlight strategic outcomes, high-level cost/benefit for renewal decision.
- Product/Platform Lead — name: (e.g., Tomas R.) — prep: discuss roadmap fit, data residency/Private options if flagged.
- ML/Inference Lead — name: (e.g., Anya P.) — prep: latency/cost metrics, model variant requests, SLOs.
- Dev/Engineering PM — name: (e.g., Luis V.) — prep: integration blockers, rollout windows, staging cadence.
- Procurement/Finance — name: (e.g., Marcus D.) — prep: forecasted spend, committed vs. actual, reserved capacity options.

Meeting agenda templates (choose based on 30/60/90 min):
- 30-minute (executive): 0–5m: Welcome & outcome framing; 5–15m: Business metrics + top 2 wins; 15–22m: Renewal health & commercial ask; 22–28m: Key roadmap asks & decisions; 28–30m: Actions & owners.
- 60-minute (operational + exec): 0–7m: Introductions & goals; 7–20m: Usage trends & cost analysis; 20–35m: Feature deep-dive or health review (tickets/incidents); 35–45m: Roadmap alignment & migration options; 45–55m: Renewal discussion & options; 55–60m: Actions & follow-ups.
- 90-minute (detailed tech + business): include breakout segments: SE-led architecture review and CSM-led success plan workshop.

Facilitation script snippets (scannable):
- Opening (CSM): "Thanks all — today’s goal is to make sure we’re aligned on outcomes for the next quarter and to confirm the path for renewal conversations. I’ll surface metrics, then we’ll tackle blockers and close with a proposal for next steps."
- Redirecting (when discussion derails): "This is a valuable discussion — can we park this in the follow-up ticket (JIRA-XXXX) and spend the remaining time on the items we committed to cover today? I’ll make sure the SE follows up."
- Handling pricing pushback: "I hear the concern on unit cost. Two levers we can look at: reserved capacity for predictable unit economics, or optimized batching/quantization suggestions from our Optimize team. If you’re open, we can model both options and share a 2-week impact estimate."
- Closing (to align asks): "To summarize, we agreed on A, B, and C. Owners are X (by date), Y (by date). I’ll circulate minutes and an action tracker within 24 hours. If there’s no objection, we’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up to review the modeled renewal scenarios."

Renewal health signals & recommended playbooks (quick reference):
- Green: consistent or growing usage, low support volume — playbook: value expansion + advocacy (capturing testimonials, reference ask).
- Yellow: flat usage, some feature gaps — playbook: targeted enablement + pilot of new features, executive sponsorship touchpoint.
- Red: decreasing usage, escalations, pricing objections — playbook: immediate SE remediation, commercial concessions + timeboxed savings model, possible dedicated capacity incentive.

On-the-call roles & responsibilities (recommended):
- CSM: facilitation, outcomes alignment, action tracker owner.
- AE: commercial alignment and renewal terms discussion.
- SE/Dev Advocate: technical clarifications, post-call remediation plan.
- Customer Success Manager II / Solutions Engineer: live demos, runbook updates.

Post-meeting follow-up checklist (24–72 hours):
- Send minutes + action tracker (24h) with owners and deadlines.
- Create JIRA tickets for technical remediation and tag SE owner (48h).
- Schedule renewal modeling session with Finance if flagged (72h).
- Share short executive one-pager aligned to sponsor’s KPIs (72h).

Templates (snippets you can copy):
- Pre-read subject line: "[Company] x Redwood — QBR pre-read & requested inputs"
- Quick follow-up: "Thanks for your time today. Attached are meeting notes and the action tracker. Next sync proposed: [date]."

Open questions / To iterate on: 
- Should we surface ML inference cost-per-conversation as a standard metric in all QBRs? (pro: ties to product ROI; con: could overwhelm execs).
- Do we want a ‘health badge’ visual in slides (green/yellow/red) standardized across accounts?

Notes to self: keep scripts concise; test a 15-minute exec-only variant for high-level sponsors; pilot a renewal modeling worksheet with two customers next month and capture outcomes.

Version history: Draft 0.1 — initial structure and scripts (Priya)
